grades.quote: As mentioned in the text, waiting for a condition variable should always be done using a loop, because when the thread finishes waiting, it may not be the first to acquire the mutex.
grades.reason: Directly explains that another thread may invalidate the condition before mutex reacquisition; also explicitly discusses spurious wakeups.

grades.quote:
If there are more than one of them, they will all try to acquire the condition lock and re-check the condition; in many cases only one will be able to do anything useful (e.g., read all the data waiting in a pipe).

The rest will find the condition is no longer true and go back to sleep; it was a waste of CPU time to wake them up.
grades.reason: Explains why awakened waiters must recheck the condition and wait again when another process has consumed the available data.
Discusses reservation-based low-power polling instructions, not why condition-variable waits require a while loop.

grades.quote: Therefore, the computational steps taken by two (or more) threads will be interleaved in a quite unpredictable manner, unless the programmer has taken explicit measures to control the order of events.
grades.reason: Provides limited background on unpredictable thread interleaving and synchronization, but does not explain condition rechecking or spurious wakeups.
